Prevention: Use clean seed from reliable and inspected fields (RAB and
Crop rotation with cereals, pyrethrum or onions for at least two seasons
Respect the correct planting density (30 x 80 cm) to avoid overcrowding
For reducing water run off, plant animal feeding grasses and/or use terraces
Plant in areas where bacterial wilt hasn't occurred previously
Avoid deep ploughing as the organisms survive in the deep, cool layers of soil
Control weed hosts from solanaceous family such as nightshade
Monitoring: Inspect the crop at least two times a season:
First time should be one month after planting; Second time should be at the beginning of flowering stage
Identify infected plants by the following symptoms:
Plant wilting without much yellowing, stunting; Cut stems ooze when suspended in a glass of water
Take action when one infected plant is observed
Direct Control: Uproot and bury infected plants outside the farm
Restrictions: Chemical control of bacterial wilt is not recommended
